subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Limits of Logic: What Reasoning Can't Do
description: One-minute skill: The Limits of Logic: What Reasoning Can't Do.

hook.text: Logic can't tell you what to value. It can't derive an 'ought' from an 'is.' Hume proved that in 1739.

buildup.text: The is-ought gap: 'People are selfish' doesn't prove 'People should be selfish.' Facts don't create values.

discovery.text: Logic is a tool for reasoning from premises — but it can't choose your starting premises for you.

twist.text: Two people can use perfect logic and reach opposite conclusions — because they started with different values.

climax.text: Logic tells you IF you want X, THEN do Y. It never tells you whether X is worth wanting.

punchline.text: Logic is the map. You still have to choose the destination.

quiz.question: What is the 'is-ought gap'?
options: Facts alone can't determine values or moral claims

details.summary: Logic has inherent limits: it cannot resolve questions of value, generate new empirical facts, or fully capture the richness of human experience. Recognizing what logic cannot do is as important as knowing what it can.
details.whyItMatters: Overestimating logic leads to rationalistic arrogance; underestimating it leads to irrationalism. Understanding its boundaries enables wise application.
takeaways: Logic cannot determine values or moral principles from scratch
Empirical knowledge requires observation, not just reasoning
Human judgment, creativity, and emotion complement logic

faq.question: What are the things logic is fundamentally unable to do?
faq.answer: Logic cannot create new empirical knowledge, resolve fundamental value disagreements, or capture subjective experience. It can only evaluate reasoning given premises from other sources.

faq.question: If logic has limits, does that mean irrational approaches are equally valid?
faq.answer: No. Logic is limited but indispensable. Its limitations mean it needs to be complemented by empirical evidence, ethical reflection, and practical wisdom—not replaced by irrationalism.
